steps.note: From the template. Any body on an api/ endpoint whose type carries DataAnnotations, or implements IValidatableObject, is checked.
The handler never ran. One entry per field; the messages are .NET's DataAnnotations defaults unless the attribute sets ErrorMessage. The address and trace id are illustrative.

body.title: The credit budget is spent
body.detail: This feature is paused until the organisation tops up its credits.

steps.note: A model call inside an illustrative endpoint hit a spent budget and the app did not catch it. Other uncaught platform failures: 503 "A platform service is unavailable" or 502 "A platform service failed", each with its code.

api() never returns a failure as data: 400 ValidationError, 401 NotSignedInError, 402 BudgetExhaustedError, 403 ForbiddenError, 404 NotFoundError, NetworkError when nothing answered, ApiError otherwise. Branch on the type, never the message.
Three states, never two: a failed read is not shown as "nothing here". After any successful write through api(), every mounted useApiQuery re-reads, keeping its data on screen meanwhile.

variations.title: A path that would escape the app's address

output: Error: api("/notes"): drop the leading slash — write api("notes"). A leading slash escapes the app's address prefix and breaks the app under a path.
Error: api("api/notes"): paths are already inside api/ — write api("notes").
Error: api("https://example.com/notes"): api() calls this app's own API only. Other hosts are reached from the server, through the platform.
steps.note: Each throws at once, before any request; the three lines are three separate calls.

steps.code: try { await api("notes"); } catch (e) { console.log(e instanceof NetworkError, e.status, e.message); }
output: true 0 The app could not be reached. Check the connection and try again.
steps.note: Offline, or the app is restarting. FailedState shows it with a way to try again.
